docs.title: modsim v2 development source
docs.text: modsim runs simulated Modbus devices for development and integration testing. The current source supports profile 0.2 TM/TD input, scenarios and independent devices on a single managed Modbus TCP listener. The published 2.0.0a1 preview does not include all current managed commands; see preview notes.

docs.title: Start a managed deployment
docs.text:
From a source checkout, docker compose up -d --build runs the root examples/deployment.yaml. Unit 1 is a virtual ADAM-5017UH input module and Unit 2 is a virtual ADAM-6024 with synthetic I/O loopback. Compose publishes port 5020 on host loopback. The ADAM mappings are manual-derived candidates; simulation is not evidence of physical device behavior.

To run locally with uv, use uv run modsim up. The default deployment binds all host interfaces when run directly. See managed deployments for updates, logging, TD export, instance IDs and script permissions.

docs.title: Unconfigured demo
docs.text:
modsim --comm tcp --port 5020 starts the legacy demonstration datastore; all Unit IDs share its four Modbus tables. TCP and UDP use socket framing; UDP listens on loopback. TLS uses certificates/pymodbus.crt and certificates/pymodbus.key relative to the working directory. It does not authenticate clients. Serial supports RTU and ASCII; physical serial hardware has not been validated by the local regression suite.

The CLI rejects non-default --store and the unsupported --slaves and --context options. Run modsim --help for available options.

docs.title: Managed deployments
docs.text: The 2.0.0a2 candidate adds two-level commands for a local, single-listener deployment. These commands are not included in the published 2.0.0a1 preview. Managed commands currently require POSIX (Linux, macOS or WSL); the existing flag-based server entry point remains available on other platforms.

docs.title: Start and reconcile
docs.text:
modsim up -f examples/deployment.yaml -d
modsim ps -f examples/deployment.yaml
modsim up -f examples/deployment.yaml --dry-run
modsim up -f examples/deployment.yaml
modsim down -f examples/deployment.yaml

All commands default to examples/deployment.yaml in the current directory. up runs in the foreground on first startup; -d starts a detached process. Later up commands update that process and follow its logs; use -d to return immediately. Interrupting the original foreground process stops its deployment. Interrupting an attached up or logs --follow disconnects that viewer while the existing deployment continues. down waits for cleanup; repeating it is harmless.

Each deployment has a name, defaulting to the deployment directory name. Names identify runtimes within the current OS user. A running name cannot be taken over by another file. Keep the file path and name stable; run down before moving or renaming the deployment. Commands operate on the selected deployment, rather than discovering every deployment on the machine.

docs.title: Deployment version 2
docs.text:
version: 2
name: lab-demo
server:
  bind: 127.0.0.1
  port: 5020
devices:
  - id: adam-5017uh
    model: examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/adam-5017uh.tm.json
    parameters:
      THING_ID: urn:modsim:example:adam-5017uh
      UNIT_ID: 1
    scenario: examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/simulation/adam-5017uh.sim.json

devices may be empty. IDs and deployment names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit (maximum 64 characters). Device IDs, instantiated TD IDs and Unit IDs must each be unique within the deployment. Paths in the repository example resolve from the project root; for standalone deployments, model and scenario paths resolve relative to the deployment file. Scripts resolve relative to their scenario file. Models may also use bounded HTTPS URLs. Pin remote model revisions for repeatable runs.

Each device contains only id, model, optional parameters and optional scenario. A model must be a profile 0.2 TM. Its instantiated TD must have a stable URI id. Supply THING_ID when the TM declares that placeholder or has no id. The deployment device ID selects management operations; the TD ID identifies the Thing; Unit ID selects the device in Modbus requests. A device's TD ID cannot change during an update: remove it in one successful up, then recreate it.

parameters supplies typed TM bindings through the published shared interpreter:

  • HOST, PORT and UNIT_ID are reserved instance arguments, passed to the interpreter's host, port and unit-id API. They can also satisfy its corresponding reserved placeholders. AUTHORITY is derived; use HOST and PORT instead.
  • THING_ID supplies an explicit TD identity when the TM has no id.
  • Other keys must match TM placeholders. Missing or unused bindings are errors.
  • HOST and PORT default to the concrete listener bind address and listener port. A wildcard bind requires explicit HOST. An advertised endpoint can differ from the listener for container port mappings or proxies; no connectivity test or port forwarding is performed by export. The deployer must configure that route.
  • UNIT_ID defaults to the model declaration, or the interpreter's fallback 1. Declare it explicitly when creating multiple instances of an unbound TM.

The deployment format is a Modsim contract, not a standard TD object. TD generation uses modpoll-wot==0.2.0a2 and its bundled TD/Modbus/profile validation. There is no private TD parser or arbitrary TD patch mechanism.

Scenarios keep their existing version "1" schema, including initial, generators, bindings, seed, tick and optional local behavior scripts. Both JSON and YAML scenario documents are accepted by managed deployments. There is no duplicate initial-value field in deployment v2. Omitting a scenario produces valid static initial values from the model. Scenario state is not exported as TD defaults.

Deployment files must use the .yaml or .yml extension. YAML uses safe loading with a 1 MiB document limit, bounded nesting and JSON compatible values; aliases, duplicate keys, implicit dates and non-finite numbers are rejected. Use quoted strings where YAML scalar inference is inappropriate.

docs.title: Update and reset behavior
docs.text:
Before changing a runtime, up validates every model and scenario and initializes all new or changed candidates. An invalid candidate leaves the live device set unchanged. This guarantee covers simulator state, not external side effects in explicitly enabled Python scripts.

  • Unchanged devices retain register writes, elapsed simulation time, random state and script state. Repeating up does not rerun their initialization hooks.
  • New IDs create independent devices. Removed IDs stop their tasks. Removing the last device leaves the listener available for a subsequent up.
  • Changed model, parameters, scenario or behavior source replaces that device and resets its state. Changes are detected by content, not just file paths.
  • Listener changes require down followed by up.

Supported protocol reads/writes and synchronous hooks do not suspend while using device state. Registry replacement happens without yielding on the same event loop, keeping an entire write and its echo on one device generation. Other Unit IDs and established TCP connections remain available during updates.

modsim reset --device adam-5017uh
modsim logs

reset rebuilds that device from the last successfully applied input snapshot, including the original behavior source. It does not read pending file edits. logs prints the last 1 MiB of the deployment log; logs -f or logs --follow keeps watching. For logs, use --file examples/deployment.yaml to select a deployment; -f means follow. ps reports device IDs, TD IDs, Unit IDs, process ID and failure status as JSON.

Local Python execution requires up --allow-scripts when starting the process. Updates cannot grant script permission to a process started without it; restart with the flag. --dry-run validates candidates and checks script syntax without executing Python behavior. It reports additions, removals, replacements and kept devices without changing the runtime. Initialization hooks are only exercised during a real application of the update.

In managed mode, a periodic behavior failure takes that device offline and marks it failed in ps; other devices continue. Repeated unchanged up preserves that failure status. Use reset to retry or change the scenario and run up. The legacy flag-based startup retains its existing process-wide failure behavior.

docs.title: TD export
docs.text:
modsim export
modsim export --device adam-5017uh -o output/adam-5017uh.td.json
modsim export --running --device adam-5017uh -o output/applied.td.json

By default, modsim export writes every TD to output/ in the project root. The directory is ignored by Git. --output-dir changes the destination.

Offline export reads the deployment, instantiates its TMs and validates the TDs; it needs no running process or scenario files and never executes behavior scripts. --running exports the last successfully applied TDs, so pending file edits cannot be mistaken for the active configuration. TD export describes interfaces and advertised endpoints, not current register values or a runtime snapshot.

docs.title: Compatibility and scope
docs.text:
modsim --config ... remains available for single-device operation. Managed deployments require version 2; version "1" and the former --deployment entry point are no longer supported. YAML support is an explicit runtime dependency.

Management uses private per-user Unix sockets and locks under the OS temporary directory. It exposes no network management listener. Concurrent first starts cannot acquire the same deployment lock; a losing start reports an error and can be retried. SIGINT/SIGTERM and down close listeners, cancel device tasks and remove the socket. The lock and log files remain for safe locking and inspection. No remote API, multi-listener management, fault injection or state migration is included in this change.

Prepare pinned example inputs from the repository root with uv run python tools/fetch-models.py; see examples/model-source.yaml.

docs.title: Model-driven simulation
docs.text: The v2 source uses the published, exact modpoll-wot==0.2.0a2 dependency. Install with uv sync --all-groups. Model parsing and TM instantiation belong to that shared package; Modsim owns state and protocol execution.

docs.title: One device
docs.text:
uv run modsim --config examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/adam-5017uh.tm.json \
  --unit-id 1 --port 5020 \
  --scenario examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/simulation/adam-5017uh.sim.json

Without --port, the listener uses 502, which needs administrator rights on Linux and on macOS for 127.0.0.1; modsim then explains how to rerun with sudo or choose a port above 1023.

--config also accepts HTTPS model URLs. GitHub blob links are converted to raw file URLs. Prefer a tag or commit SHA for repeatable runs; branch URLs change. Downloads have a 15-second timeout and a 1 MiB limit, and use the shared bounded JSON loader. Only models are downloaded; no script is fetched or executed from a model. JSON-LD context URLs are vocabulary identifiers, not execution sources.

The configured runtime supports profile 0.2 integer types (16/32/64-bit, signed/unsigned), IEEE float16/32/64, fixed-capacity UTF-8 strings, register and physical scalar booleans, physical boolean arrays, legacy register bool/bool8/ bool16 arrays, register bit selectors and explicit legacy-MSB packed bit payloads. Byte and word ordering follow the shared contract; legacy packed bit numeric payloads ignore word ordering, and packed strings ignore both, matching Modpoll.

Initialization, script updates, generators and Modbus writes use the same codec. Integer-wire multipliers are inverted with exact rational arithmetic: values that require fractional raw integers or overflow are rejected instead of truncated. Negative factors are supported. A zero factor can only encode engineering zero, using raw zero. IEEE values use their representable wire precision; startup reports and device.get return the decoded value. Model constraints apply after quantization too: an unrepresentable exact const is rejected. Numeric initial values use bounded candidates and arithmetic, not enumeration of 32/64-bit ranges. Complex constraints may require an explicit initial value/default/enum.

Strings must fit their UTF-8 byte capacity, use zero padding and cannot end in NUL (consumers strip trailing NULs). Physical bit arrays have their declared length. Legacy register bool arrays retain the consumer's byte/LSB layout and preserve unused padding. No engineering-unit conversion is guessed for raw ADAM channels. Profile 0.2 is required; the unconfigured demonstration is unchanged.

docs.title: Managed deployments
docs.text:
For repeatable startup and runtime updates, use deployment version 2 and modsim up. See managed deployments for the YAML contract, TM parameters, dynamic device lifecycle and TD export. The ADAM lab example starts two independent devices on one listener:

uv run modsim up -f examples/deployment.yaml

Paths in deployment files are relative to the deployment directory; scenario script paths are relative to the scenario file. Unit IDs and TD identities must be unique. Unknown addresses or Unit IDs never inherit another device's state.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Version "1" fields:

Field Meaning initial Property-name/value overrides tick Update interval in seconds, default 1, minimum 0.001 seed Per-instance random seed, default 0 generators Property-name to generator specification bindings Target property to source property for synthetic loopback writePolicy hold (default) or overwrite for generated properties script Local Python file parameters Script values exposed as device.parameters

Generators: constant (value); sine (center, amplitude, positive period); ramp (start, rate, minimum, maximum, clamped to bounds); noise (minimum, maximum, uniform seeded noise). Integer-property noise uses integer sampling to preserve the full 64-bit range. Numeric generators round to the nearest integer for integer model properties. Boolean channels can use constant values, bindings or scripts. All updates must satisfy the model's schema and raw encoding bounds. Unknown properties are errors. Binding chains and cycles are rejected; use a script for ordered dependencies.

Initialization order: model defaults/type fallback → scenario initial → CLI initial → script initialize → first dynamic update at elapsed 0. --initial and --initial-file remain available for single-device runs. Single-device startup logs include the final initialized values; raw values are synthetic unless the contribution explicitly documents their source.

On each tick: generators → script tick → bindings. Modbus writes validate the whole request, then run on_write and bindings before responding. Invalid write requests or failed write hooks roll back register changes. Partial register writes re-decode every overlapping property, including properties whose first register was not touched. Batch updates and alias constraints are checked before commit. Bit-field updates preserve neighboring bits. Protocol writes may not change read-only/reserved bits; a writable bit sharing a register with read-only bits can be changed while preserving those bits. Reads that would expose a write-only field are rejected, while FC5/6 write echoes remain supported. Model read-only measurements may be changed internally but cannot be written by clients. hold stops a generator for a property after a valid client write until restart; overwrite permits the next tick to replace it. Scripts define their own write response and may deliberately overwrite values.

docs.title: Local Python behaviors
docs.text:
uv run modsim --config examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/adam-5017uh.tm.json \
  --scenario examples/models/advantech/adam-5017uh/simulation/adam-5017uh-scripted-analog-input.sim.json --allow-scripts

Optional synchronous hooks:

def initialize(device):
    device.set("AI0_RAW", 100)


def tick(device, elapsed, dt):
    device.set("AI0_RAW", 100 + int(elapsed) % 100)


def on_write(device, changes):
    if "AO0_RAW" in changes:
        device.set("AI0_RAW", changes["AO0_RAW"])

Use get(name), set(name, value) and set_many({...}). Batch updates validate all values before changing cells. Hooks run on the server event loop and must not block; async hooks are rejected. Python is ordinary local code, enabled explicitly by --allow-scripts. Each device loads its own module instance. In single-device --config mode, periodic behavior errors stop the server. In managed mode, an error takes only that device offline and is reported by ps. SIGINT/SIGTERM cancel updates and close the server.

The sample loopback is an explicit synthetic assumption, not a claim that real ADAM hardware automatically connects AO to AI or DO to DI. No fault injection, recording/replay, multi-listener runtime or remote behavior execution is included.

Prepare pinned example inputs from the repository root with uv run python tools/fetch-models.py; see examples/model-source.yaml.

docs.title: privileged_port_hint(port)
docs.text:
Explain how to listen on a port the operating system reserves.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
def privileged_port_hint(port: Any) -> str:
    """Explain how to listen on a port the operating system reserves."""
    return (
        f"Port {port} needs administrator rights on this system. Run the same "
        'command with sudo; with uvx that is sudo "$(command -v uvx)" followed by '
        "the rest of the command. Or listen on a port above 1023, for example "
        "--port 5020, and point the client at it (modpoll --tcp-port 5020)."
    )

docs.title: require_bindable(host, port, kind=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
docs.text:
Fail early with a clear message when binding needs elevated rights.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
def require_bindable(host: str, port: Any, kind: int = socket.SOCK_STREAM) -> None:
    """Fail early with a clear message when binding needs elevated rights."""
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, kind) as probe:
        try:
            probe.bind((host, int(port)))
        except PermissionError as exc:
            raise OSError(privileged_port_hint(port)) from exc
        except OSError:
            # Occupied ports and other failures are reported by the server itself.
            return

docs.title: run_async_server(args) async
docs.text:
Run server.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
async def run_async_server(args: Any) -> Any:
    """Run server."""
    txt = f"Start ASYNC server, listening on {args.port} - {args.comm}"
    _logger.info(txt)
    server: Any
    if args.comm == "tcp":
        address: tuple[str, int] = (
            getattr(args, "bind", None)
            or ("127.0.0.1" if getattr(args, "runtimes", None) else ""),
            args.port,
        )
        require_bindable(address[0], args.port)
        server = ModbusTcpServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        if hasattr(args, "runtimes"):
            from .runtime import RuntimeContext

            server.context = RuntimeContext(args.runtimes)
        tasks = []
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus TCP listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            tasks = [
                asyncio.create_task(device.run())
                for device in getattr(args, "runtimes", [])
            ]
            await asyncio.gather(server.serving, *tasks)
        finally:
            for task in tasks:
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    elif args.comm == "udp":
        address = ("127.0.0.1", args.port)
        require_bindable(address[0], args.port, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        server = ModbusUdpServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus UDP listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            await server.serving
        finally:
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    elif args.comm == "serial":
        await StartAsyncSerialServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            port=args.port,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        return None
    elif args.comm == "tls":
        address = ("", args.port)
        require_bindable(address[0], args.port)
        # Create SSL context from cert and key files
        sslctx = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH)
        sslctx.load_cert_chain(
            certfile="certificates/pymodbus.crt",
            keyfile="certificates/pymodbus.key",
        )

        server = ModbusTlsServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
            sslctx=sslctx,
        )
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus TLS listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            await server.serving
        finally:
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown communication type: {args.comm}")

docs.title: setup_server(args)
docs.text:
Run server setup.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
def setup_server(args: Any) -> Any:
    """Run server setup."""
    # The datastores only respond to the addresses that are initialized
    # If you initialize a DataBlock to addresses of 0x00 to 0xFF, a request to
    # 0x100 will respond with an invalid address exception.
    # This is because many devices exhibit this kind of behavior (but not all)
    if getattr(args, "config", None):
        from .deployment import configure_devices

        args.context = configure_devices(args)
        _logger.info(
            "Model initialization: %s",
            json.dumps(args.model_initialization, sort_keys=True),
        )
    if not args.context:
        _logger.info("Create datastore")
        # build your payload
        co_builder = BinaryPayloadBuilder(byteorder=Endian.BIG, wordorder=Endian.BIG)
        # address=0, bytes=3
        for _ in range(3):
            # The bits within each byte are big-endian
            # The coils status (from the first position) = [1,0,1,0,0,0,0,1]
            co_builder.add_bits([True, False, True, False, False, False, False, True])

        hr_builder = BinaryPayloadBuilder(byteorder=Endian.BIG, wordorder=Endian.BIG)
        # address=0, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(1)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(2)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(3)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(4)
        # address=8, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-1)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-2)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-3)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-4)
        # address=16, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_uint(12345678)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_uint(12345678)
        # address=24, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_int(-12345678)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_int(-12345678)
        # address=32, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_float(12.34)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_float(-12.34)
        # address=40, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_64bit_uint(12345678900)
        # address=48, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_64bit_int(-12345678900)
        # address=56, bytes=16
        hr_builder.add_64bit_float(123.45)
        hr_builder.add_64bit_float(-123.45)
        # address=72, bytes=?
        hr_builder.add_string("this is a string")

        # use that payload in the data store
        co_values = co_builder.to_coils()
        hr_values = hr_builder.to_registers()
        args.context = SimDevice(
            id=0,
            simdata=(
                [SimData(0, values=co_values, datatype=DataType.BITS)],
                [SimData(10000, values=co_values, datatype=DataType.BITS)],
                [SimData(40000, values=hr_values, datatype=DataType.REGISTERS)],
                [SimData(30000, values=hr_values, datatype=DataType.REGISTERS)],
            ),
        )

    # initialize the server information
    # If you don't set this or any fields, they are defaulted to empty strings.
    args.identity = ModbusDeviceIdentification(
        info_name={
            "VendorName": "Pymodbus",
            "ProductCode": "PM",
            "VendorUrl": "https://github.com/riptideio/pymodbus/",
            "ProductName": "Pymodbus Server",
            "ModelName": "Pymodbus Server",
        }
    )
    return args

docs.title: RuntimeManager
docs.text:
Own live devices and their tasks; commits never yield to protocol access.

Source code in modsim/management.py 
class RuntimeManager:
    """Own live devices and their tasks; commits never yield to protocol access."""

    def __init__(self, allow_scripts: bool = False) -> None:
        self.allow_scripts = allow_scripts
        self.deployment: Deployment | None = None
        self.context = RuntimeContext([])
        self.instances: dict[str, Instance] = {}
        self.devices: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()

    def plan(self, desired: Deployment) -> dict:
        if self.deployment:
            if desired.path != self.deployment.path:
                raise ValueError("deployment name belongs to a different file")
            if desired.name != self.deployment.name:
                raise ValueError("deployment name cannot change")
            if (desired.bind, desired.port) != (
                self.deployment.bind,
                self.deployment.port,
            ):
                raise ValueError("listener changed; run down before up")
        added, replaced, kept = [], [], []
        for key, item in desired.instances.items():
            old = self.instances.get(key)
            if old is None:
                added.append(key)
            elif item.td["id"] != old.td["id"]:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{key}: TD id changed; remove the device before recreating"
                )
            elif item.fingerprint != old.fingerprint:
                replaced.append(key)
            else:
                kept.append(key)
        return {
            "added": added,
            "replaced": replaced,
            "removed": sorted(self.instances.keys() - desired.instances.keys()),
            "kept": kept,
        }

    async def apply(self, desired: Deployment, dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
        plan = self.plan(desired)
        # Only changed candidates initialize; repeated up cannot rerun live hooks.
        candidates = {
            key: desired.instances[key].build(self.allow_scripts, preview=dry_run)
            for key in plan["added"] + plan["replaced"]
        }
        if dry_run:
            return plan
        retired = [self.tasks[key] for key in plan["removed"] + plan["replaced"]]
        next_devices = {
            key: candidates[key] if key in candidates else self.devices[key]
            for key in desired.instances
        }
        next_tasks = {key: self.tasks[key] for key in plan["kept"]}
        for key, device in candidates.items():
            next_tasks[key] = asyncio.create_task(self.run_device(key, device))
        # The supported datastore operations and hooks do not suspend. Swapping
        # this registry in the same event loop is also atomic across write echoes.
        self.context.devices = {
            device.unit_id: device
            for key, device in next_devices.items()
            if key not in self.errors or key in candidates
        }
        for task in retired:
            task.cancel()
        self.instances = desired.instances
        self.devices = next_devices
        self.tasks = next_tasks
        self.errors = {
            key: self.errors[key] for key in plan["kept"] if key in self.errors
        }
        self.deployment = desired
        await asyncio.gather(*retired, return_exceptions=True)
        LOG.info("Deployment applied: %s", plan)
        return plan

    async def run_device(self, key: str, device: Any) -> None:
        try:
            await device.run()
        except Exception as exc:
            self.errors[key] = str(exc)
            # An invalid behavior must not keep serving apparently healthy data.
            self.context.devices.pop(device.unit_id, None)
            LOG.exception("Device %s failed; other devices remain online", key)

    async def reset(self, key: str) -> dict:
        if key not in self.instances:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown device: {key}")
        candidate = self.instances[key].build(self.allow_scripts)
        old = self.tasks[key]
        self.context.devices[candidate.unit_id] = candidate
        self.devices[key] = candidate
        self.tasks[key] = asyncio.create_task(self.run_device(key, candidate))
        self.errors.pop(key, None)
        old.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(old, return_exceptions=True)
        return {"reset": key}

    def status(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "running": True,
            "name": self.deployment.name if self.deployment else None,
            "source": str(self.deployment.path) if self.deployment else None,
            "pid": os.getpid(),
            "devices": [
                {
                    "id": key,
                    "tdId": self.instances[key].td["id"],
                    "unitId": device.unit_id,
                    "state": "failed" if key in self.errors else "running",
                    "error": self.errors.get(key),
                }
                for key, device in self.devices.items()
            ],
        }

    async def close(self) -> None:
        self.context.devices = {}
        for task in self.tasks.values():
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*self.tasks.values(), return_exceptions=True)

def paths(name: str) -> tuple[Path, Path, Path]:
    """Use a per-user private directory and a short, name-derived socket path."""
    if os.name != "posix":
        raise ValueError("managed commands currently require POSIX (Linux/macOS/WSL)")
    root = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"modsim-{os.getuid()}"
    root.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    info = root.lstat()
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != os.getuid():
        raise ValueError("unsafe runtime directory")
    if stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != 0o700:
        raise ValueError("runtime directory must have permissions 0700")
    key = hashlib.sha256(name.encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
    return root / f"{key}.sock", root / f"{key}.lock", root / f"{key}.log"

async def serve(
    path: Path, allow_scripts: bool = False, *, detached: bool = False
) -> None:
    """Hold the deployment lock through listener and task shutdown."""
    import fcntl

    desired = await asyncio.to_thread(load_deployment, path)
    socket_path, lock_path, log_path = paths(desired.name)
    with lock_path.open("a") as lease:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(lease, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                "deployment is already starting or running; retry up"
            ) from exc
        manager = RuntimeManager(allow_scripts)
        stop = asyncio.Event()
        server: Any = ModbusTcpServer(
            context=SimDevice(
                id=0,
                simdata=[SimData(0, datatype=DataType.INVALID)],
            ),
            address=(desired.bind, desired.port),
        )
        server.context = manager.context
        control = None
        handlers: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        signals = []
        file_handler = None
        if not detached:
            file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path)
            os.chmod(log_path, 0o600)
            logging.getLogger().addHandler(file_handler)

        async def handle(
            reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter
        ) -> None:
            task = asyncio.current_task()
            if task is not None:
                handlers.add(task)
            try:
                async with manager.lock:
                    payload = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readline(), 5)
                    message = json.loads(payload)
                    if message.get("source") != str(desired.path):
                        raise ValueError("deployment name belongs to a different file")
                    action = message.get("action")
                    if action == "up":
                        if message.get("allow_scripts") and not manager.allow_scripts:
                            raise ValueError(
                                "script permission requires down, then up --allow-scripts"
                            )
                        candidate = await asyncio.to_thread(
                            load_deployment, desired.path
                        )
                        result = await manager.apply(
                            candidate, bool(message.get("dry_run"))
                        )
                    elif action == "ps":
                        result = manager.status()
                    elif action == "reset":
                        result = await manager.reset(message.get("device", ""))
                    elif action == "export":
                        result = {
                            "tds": {
                                key: item.td for key, item in manager.instances.items()
                            }
                        }
                    elif action == "down":
                        result = {"stopping": True}
                        stop.set()
                    else:
                        raise ValueError("unknown management action")
                response = result
            except Exception as exc:
                response = {"error": str(exc)}
            try:
                writer.write(json.dumps(response).encode() + b"\n")
                await writer.drain()
            finally:
                writer.close()
                with suppress(ConnectionError):
                    await writer.wait_closed()
                if task is not None:
                    handlers.discard(task)

        try:
            await manager.apply(desired)
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(f"cannot listen on {desired.bind}:{desired.port}")
            # The lease proves that a leftover socket cannot belong to a live owner.
            socket_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            control = await asyncio.start_unix_server(
                handle, path=str(socket_path), limit=MAX_REQUEST
            )
            os.chmod(socket_path, 0o600)
            for signum in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
                loop.add_signal_handler(signum, stop.set)
                signals.append(signum)
            LOG.info(
                "Deployment %s ready at %s:%s", desired.name, desired.bind, desired.port
            )
            await stop.wait()
        finally:
            if control:
                control.close()
                await control.wait_closed()
            for task in list(handlers):
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*handlers, return_exceptions=True)
            for signum in signals:
                loop.remove_signal_handler(signum)
            await manager.close()
            await server.shutdown()
            socket_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            if file_handler:
                logging.getLogger().removeHandler(file_handler)
                file_handler.close()

class DeploymentLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):  # type: ignore[no-any-unimported]
    """Reject aliases and duplicate keys rather than expanding ambiguous YAML."""

    def compose_node(self, parent: Any, index: Any) -> Any:
        if self.check_event(yaml.AliasEvent):
            raise ValueError("YAML aliases are unsupported")
        depth = getattr(self, "deployment_depth", 0)
        if depth >= 64:
            raise ValueError("deployment nesting exceeds 64 containers")
        self.deployment_depth = depth + 1
        try:
            return super().compose_node(parent, index)
        finally:
            self.deployment_depth = depth

    def construct_mapping(self, node: Any, deep: bool = False) -> dict:
        result = {}
        for key_node, value_node in node.value:
            key = self.construct_object(key_node, deep=deep)
            if not isinstance(key, str):
                raise ValueError("YAML object keys must be strings")
            if key in result:
                raise ValueError(f"duplicate YAML key: {key}")
            result[key] = self.construct_object(value_node, deep=deep)
        return result

class Instance:
    id: str

    def build(self, allow_scripts: bool = False, *, preview: bool = False) -> Any:
        """Construct isolated state from this snapshot, without reopening inputs."""
        from .deployment import apply_scenario
        from .wot import configure

        if self.script_source is not None:
            if not allow_scripts:
                raise ValueError("Python behavior scripts require --allow-scripts")
            if preview:
                compile(self.script_source, self.script_path or "<behavior>", "exec")
        args = Namespace(
            prepared_model=self.model,
            initial_file=None,
            initial=[],
            scenario=None,
            scenario_spec=copy.deepcopy(self.scenario),
            script=None if preview else self.script_path,
            script_source=self.script_source,
            allow_scripts=allow_scripts,
        )
        configure(args)
        args.runtime.name = self.id
        apply_scenario(args)
        return args.runtime

def deployment_root(path: Path) -> Path:
    """Use the repository root for checked-in examples, config directory otherwise."""
    for parent in path.parent.parents:
        marker = parent / ".git"
        if marker.is_file() or (marker.is_dir() and any(marker.iterdir())):
            return parent
    marker = path.parent / ".git"
    if marker.is_file() or (marker.is_dir() and any(marker.iterdir())):
        return path.parent
    return path.parent

def load_deployment(path: Path, *, include_scenarios: bool = True) -> Deployment:
    """Resolve and validate every instance before the runtime can be changed."""
    path = path.resolve()
    if path.suffix.lower() not in (".yaml", ".yml"):
        raise ValueError("deployment file must use .yaml or .yml")
    spec = read_yaml(path)
    validate(spec, MANIFEST)
    name = spec.get("name", path.parent.name)
    validate({"name": name}, obj({"name": IDENTIFIER}, ("name",)))
    bind = spec.get("server", {}).get("bind", "127.0.0.1")
    port = spec.get("server", {}).get("port", 5020)
    root = deployment_root(path)
    instances: dict[str, Instance] = {}
    units: set[int] = set()
    identities: set[str] = set()
    for item in spec["devices"]:
        key = item["id"]
        if key in instances:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate device id: {key}")
        source = item["model"]
        if not source.startswith("https://"):
            source = local_path(root, source)
        document = model_document(source)
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: model must be an object")
        types = document.get("@type", [])
        if isinstance(types, str):
            types = [types]
        if "tm:ThingModel" not in types:
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: deployment v2 requires a TM; use --config for TD")
        parameters = dict(item.get("parameters", {}))
        if "AUTHORITY" in parameters:
            raise ValueError(
                "use HOST and PORT; AUTHORITY is derived by the interpreter"
            )
        # A TM need not declare a Thing ID. An explicit instance binding may
        # provide it without changing the reusable model or inventing identity.
        if "THING_ID" in parameters and "id" not in document:
            document = copy.deepcopy(document)
            document["id"] = "{{THING_ID}}"
        host = parameters.pop("HOST", None)
        if host is None:
            if bind in ("0.0.0.0", "::", "*"):
                raise ValueError(f"{key}: wildcard listener requires parameters.HOST")
            host = bind
        instance_port = parameters.pop("PORT", port)
        unit = parameters.pop("UNIT_ID", None)
        if not isinstance(host, str):
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: HOST must be a string")
        td = export_td(
            document, host=host, port=instance_port, unit_id=unit, parameters=parameters
        )
        if len(canonical(td)) > MAX_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: generated TD exceeds 1 MiB")
        model = parse_model(td)
        identity = td.get("id")
        if not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity:
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: TM must instantiate a stable TD id")
        if identity in identities or model.unit_id in units:
            raise ValueError(f"{key}: duplicate TD id or Unit ID")
        units.add(model.unit_id)
        identities.add(identity)
        scenario = {}
        script_path, script_source = None, None
        if include_scenarios and item.get("scenario"):
            scene_path = Path(local_path(root, item["scenario"]))
            scenario = read_yaml(scene_path)
            validate(scenario, SCENARIO)
            if scenario.get("script"):
                script_path = local_path(scene_path.parent, scenario["script"])
                with Path(script_path).open("rb") as stream:
                    script_source = stream.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)
                if len(script_source) > MAX_BYTES:
                    raise ValueError("script exceeds 1 MiB")
                # Resolved script is supplied separately to apply_scenario.
                scenario = {k: v for k, v in scenario.items() if k != "script"}
        fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(
            canonical([item, document, td, scenario, script_path])
            + (script_source or b"")
        ).hexdigest()
        instances[key] = Instance(
            key, td, model, fingerprint, scenario, script_path, script_source
        )
    return Deployment(path, name, bind, port, instances)

def read_yaml(path: Path) -> dict:
    """Read JSON or safe YAML with bounded size, depth and JSON-compatible values."""
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".json":
        value = load_document(path)
    else:
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            payload = stream.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)
        if len(payload) > MAX_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("deployment exceeds 1 MiB")
        try:
            value = yaml.load(payload, Loader=DeploymentLoader)
        except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: invalid YAML: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected an object")
    try:
        canonical(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, RecursionError) as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected finite JSON-compatible values") from exc
    return value
